question: Should exec denylist policy permanently union tools.exec.denylist with each host's exec-approvals.json denylist, with matches requiring one-shot human approval across gateway, node, and macOS companion execution?
rationale: This establishes a new persisted security contract and authority model across independently updated execution hosts; tests cannot determine which policy surface maintainers intend to own permanently.

options.title: Accept the dual-layer union
options.body: Keep both requested configuration and host-local STOP rules, require deny-anywhere semantics, and finish mixed-version plus integrated companion proof before merge.

options.title: Make the host file authoritative
options.body: Remove the tools.exec denylist surface and keep STOP rules solely in host approval policy, reducing configuration duplication at the cost of centralized agent configuration.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Do not merge until maintainers define a different deny-by-exception security model with a narrower cross-host contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the dual-layer union
recommendation.body: Keep both requested configuration and host-local STOP rules, require deny-anywhere semantics, and finish mixed-version plus integrated companion proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history and the PR discussion connect steipete to exec-approval policy and the required security-boundary decision.
